Subject: Quantified consumption curve + $/1M target — post-demo recap

Maya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can get you an apples-to-apples hosted pricing package.

TL;DR: please confirm (1) expected steady-state monthly token volume, (2) expected 99th-percentile TPS during peak windows, and (3) your target $/1M token band for procurement. I attached a simple consumption-estimate (xlsx) that maps a few traffic shapes to hosted-band recommendations.

What we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: clinical documentation summarization + search enrichment (short prompts, multi-turn).
- Current pilot: ~12M tokens/month observed (Oct) with periodic morning spikes.
- Desired initial commercial band: keep OPEX < ~$5k/mo while supporting growth.

Preliminary pricing guidance (hosted API):
- Pay-as-you-go baseline: $4.25 / 1M tokens
- Committed band (3–6 month commit): $2.75 — $3.50 / 1M tokens depending on volume and SLAs
- Burst/peak allowance: small burst blocks available for short 60–120s windows; longer sustained spikes recommend reserved capacity.

Operational sizing notes we used in estimate:
- Baseline concurrency assumption: 40–60 TPS sustained for user-facing calls
- Peak shaping: 150–250 TPS for short windows (up to 2 minutes) is common for similar customers

Asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm the numbers in the attached spreadsheet (monthly tokens by month, and a realistic 99th-tps figure for your busiest 5–10 minute windows).
2) If the $/1M target you have in procurement is < $3.50, flag that number — we can model a committed slab to hit that.
3) Would you like us to run a short burst test next week to validate 99th TPS behavior on our hosted stack?

I can loop in pricing (Karthik) and solutions if you want a short call to walk the spreadsheet live.

— Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Jonas — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side (rough ballpark numbers):

1) Monthly volume: baseline 12M tokens currently; planning a product ramp to ~36M tokens/mo over 4–6 months if early results hold (we'll control ramp by feature flags).
2) Peak shape: our busiest windows are morning ingestion and batch-syncs. We typically see short spikes up to ~200 TPS (99th ~180–220 TPS) for 30–90s, while steady interactive load is ~35–50 TPS.
3) Budget: procurement is targeting $3k–6k/mo in the first 3 months (we can flex if committed discounts make it worth it). The $/1M target is something they asked for as a negotiation anchor — ideally in the $2.50–$3.50 / 1M range but we need to see the tradeoffs.

On the burst test: yes, we'd take a quick smoke test next week. Also please confirm how prefix/KV caching could reduce token burn on our long-running multi-turn flows — that's important for our unit economics.

— Maya
Head of ML Ops | Luminar Bio

Maya — perfect, thanks for the detail. A couple quick clarifications and how we can help to fit the $/1M target:

1) Caching & token burn: prefix/KV caching can materially reduce token consumption for multi-turn sessions. For summarization flows we commonly see 10–40% token reduction depending on prompt reuse. We'll model cache hit assumptions in the attached pricing-teaser and in your spreadsheet.

2) For your ramp profile the two levers to hit the $2.50–$3.50 / 1M range are: (a) a 3–6 month committed slab (volume tier), or (b) a hybrid: lower commit + burst credits. Example structures we can model:
   - 12–25M/mo commit → $3.25 / 1M, 30-day cancellation window
   - 25–50M/mo commit → $2.75 / 1M + 5% CDN credit for embedding-heavy traffic

3) Peak TPS handling: hosted can absorb 200–300 TPS bursts for short windows automatically; for repeated/long spikes we recommend a small Reserved node to keep 99th SLOs predictable. We can quote reserved capacity vs committed slab in the same model.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll run two pricing scenarios in the spreadsheet: conservative (12M→18M ramp) and aggressive (12M→36M ramp) and show the $/1M and monthly outcomes for pay-as-you-go vs 3-month committed slabs.
- Karthik, can you confirm if we can offer a one-time uplift credit (first 30 days) to help Luminar hit internal pilot targets?
- Schedule a 30-min burst test Wed 10/28 or Thu 10/29 (you pick). We’ll coordinate with Dev/Infra.

Attaching quick pricing teaser — should help procurement have something to review internally.

— Jonas
